audit_summary.summary: ARIA's core owner path (review → confirm → approve → record payment) works and the surface is polished, but it is not launch-ready as-is. Five P0 blockers, all XS–M effort: (1) live production still shows the wrong zero-start-value bills (A102 ฿33,235, A103 ฿39,035 with a recorded payment) and the w47/g39 repair tooling is not deployed; (2) a retired meter's end_value is ignored when it also has an in-cycle reading, silently under-billing meter swaps; (3) the next cycle's base is recomputed live and cutoffs stay editable after approval, allowing double-billing; (4) write() reports failure when a payment/email succeeded but the refresh failed, inviting duplicate payments; (5) the Guest top bar overflows on 320–375px phones — the judges' entry point. Beyond these, money-flow UX is the main risk: mid-cycle move-outs go unbilled, emails/QR ignore partial payments, date defaults ignore the selected cycle, pre-cutoff approval and stale recipients are not warned, and no usage anomaly flag exists. Guest PII exposure is accepted for test data but must be closed before real tenants. Design/mobile issues are mostly polish (native dialogs, tiny Thai text, modal and breakpoint handling). Verdict: CONDITIONAL_PASS — launch after the five P0 fixes plus a deploy from main; schedule P1 money items next.
top_risks: Wrong approved bills and a ฿39,035 payment visible to judges in live Guest view until w47 is deployed and data corrected (WEB-001)
Silent billing errors on meter swaps and after post-approval data/cutoff changes (WEB-002, WEB-003, WEB-009)
Duplicate payments/emails when a write succeeds but the refresh fails (WEB-004)
Lost revenue on mid-cycle move-outs; tenants asked to pay full total after partial payment (WEB-007, WEB-008)
Tenant PII readable by anonymous Guest once real data is entered (WEB-006)
Judge-facing Guest view broken on common phone widths (WEB-005)

issues.title: Retired meter's end_value is ignored when the meter also has a confirmed reading in the same cycle → units silently lost
issues.user_journey: Owner replaces a meter mid-cycle (ปลด old with end value, add new same day) → approves the cycle's bill
issues.description: typeUsage takes curr from the last confirmed in-cycle reading and only falls back to the retired meter's end_value when there is no in-cycle reading. If the robot read the old meter earlier in the cycle, the units between that reading and the removal reading are never billed, and the next cycle excludes the retired meter entirely.
issues.user_impact: Silent under-billing on every mid-cycle meter swap that had an earlier in-cycle reading; the bill looks complete, so the owner has no cue. Meter replacement is a documented flow ("เปลี่ยนมิเตอร์ = ปลดตัวเก่าแล้วเพิ่มตัวใหม่วันเดียวกัน").

issues.expected_behavior: October water = 150 + 30 = 180; end_value lower than the last confirmed reading is rejected at retire time.
steps_to_reproduce: In ?mock, confirm W-101-01 readings 900 (29 Sep) and 1000 (10 Oct)
Rooms → 101 → ปลด W-101-01 with date 20 Oct and end value 1050
Add W-101-02 installed 20 Oct start 0, confirm a reading of 30
Bills → October → room 101: water units = 130 instead of 180

evidence.notes: logic.js:137-139 — curr = inCycle ? confirmed_value : null; end_value used only if curr == null. State agent verified by script. Next cycle: meterOverlaps excludes the meter retired before range.from.

issues.root_cause: end_value treated as a fallback rather than as the latest reading of a retired meter.
issues.recommended_fix: In typeUsage: if m.retired_at && m.retired_at <= range.to && m.end_value != null, curr = max(inCycle?.confirmed_value ?? -Inf, end_value). In retireMeter (and ideally a DB check), reject end_value < last confirmed value. Add a logic.test.mjs case for the swap scenario.

issues.title: Next cycle's base is recomputed live instead of pinned to the approved invoice; cutoff can be changed after approval → double- or under-billing
issues.user_journey: Owner approves October, later edits October's cutoff (or confirms/corrects a late October reading) → November preview
issues.description: The base for cycle N+1 is 'last confirmed reading ≤ range.from' computed from current data, not the curr stored on cycle N's approved invoice. saveCycle has no guard against cycles that already have approved invoices, and approve_invoices only inserts the cutoff if no row exists.

issues.actual_behavior: Approve Oct with cutoff 31 Oct billed to 200; set Oct cutoff to 25 Oct → Nov preview 150 units instead of 100 (50 double-billed). Same when a late cycle-N reading is confirmed/corrected after N is approved.
issues.expected_behavior: Changing a cutoff for a cycle with approved invoices (N or N+1) is refused or explicitly warned; N+1 base = approved invoice segment curr, and a mismatch is flagged.
steps_to_reproduce: In ?mock, approve October for a room with readings 100 (≤ 30 Sep), 150 (25 Oct), 200 (31 Oct)
Settings → รอบบิล → set October cutoff to 25 Oct and save (accepted)
Bills → November preview for that room: base 150, units counted from 150 although October already billed to 200

evidence.notes: logic.js:135 base = lastConfirmed(d <= range.from); app.js:1094-1102 saveCycle only checks ordering vs adjacent cutoffs; migrations/20261003000100_invoices.sql:64 'on conflict (cycle) do nothing'. State agent verified by script.

issues.root_cause: Approved invoices are not treated as the source of truth for the following cycle's base; cycle cutoffs are mutable after approval.
issues.recommended_fix: 1) saveCycle: refuse (or require explicit confirm + reason) when cycle N or N+1 has approved invoices. 2) typeUsage: when the previous cycle has an approved invoice for the room, use its detail.segments[type][].curr as base and add a reason/flag if it differs from the live base. 3) Optionally enforce in a DB trigger on billing_cycles.

issues.title: write() reports failure when the write succeeded but the refresh failed → duplicate payments / duplicate emails
issues.page: Bill modal (payments), Bills (send email), all write actions
issues.user_journey: Owner on a flaky mobile connection records a ฿500 payment → toast says it failed → saves again
issues.description: write() wraps both fn() and reload() in one try. If the insert succeeds but loadAll throws, the user sees "บันทึกไม่สำเร็จ: …" and the bill modal still shows the old balance, so re-submitting records a second payment. Payments have no idempotency key; the same applies to sending emails (resend duplicates to tenants).
issues.user_impact: Money records overstated (two ฿500 rows, status ชำระแล้ว) and tenants can receive duplicate bill emails; the error message actively misleads.
issues.actual_behavior: Row inserted; toast "บันทึกไม่สำเร็จ: ต่อเน็ตไม่ได้"; modal still "ค้าง ฿997"; second save inserts a duplicate.
issues.expected_behavior: "บันทึกแล้ว แต่รีเฟรชไม่สำเร็จ — กดรีเฟรชก่อนทำต่อ"; duplicate submit rejected server-side.
steps_to_reproduce: In ?mock, make api.loadAll throw once (devtools override)
Open an approved bill → บันทึกรับเงิน ฿500 → confirm
Observe failure toast and unchanged balance
Submit again → two ฿500 payments listed

evidence.notes: app.js:83-95 try { await fn(); state.editing=null; await reload(); … } catch { toast('บันทึกไม่สำเร็จ…') }. State agent verified in browser (mock).

issues.root_cause: Write outcome and refresh outcome are conflated; no idempotency for payments/email sends.
issues.recommended_fix: Split write(): after fn() resolves, mark success; wrap reload() separately and on failure toast 'บันทึกแล้ว · โหลดข้อมูลใหม่ไม่สำเร็จ' with a reload action, return true. Add a client-generated idempotency key (uuid) column with a unique index on payments; disable the submit button until the modal is refreshed.
acceptance_criteria: Forced reload failure after a successful payment shows a success+refresh-failed message
Re-submitting the same payment form is rejected (unique idempotency key)
Bill modal reflects the new balance after a manual refresh
